### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **11** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-approvals`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/service-analytics`, `@objectstack/service-print`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **63** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**31** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `updateData (4 routes)`
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **192** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c3effc4229c8d0ff287174db4ef1086f4357c1c9` — the merge of head `d0668d12a8e6ec3a02a2efd20560e87fa6f90cba` into base `d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c3effc4229c8d0ff287174db4ef1086f4357c1c9 && git checkout c3effc4229c8d0ff287174db4ef1086f4357c1c9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6 d0668d12a8e6ec3a02a2efd20560e87fa6f90cba && git checkout -B drift-repro d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6 && git merge --no-ff d0668d12a8e6ec3a02a2efd20560e87fa6f90cba

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d576509c80575197b3218aeb1f55884e5ed06ea6` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 first review (full) · REWORK** · Head-sha: `d50700b3468c39cc4a5dd8871f050c1e673e97bb` · card #34699 rows 1, 3, 4, 5 (`Fixes #34699`) · read 2026-11-17T13:23Z

There is no earlier L1 or contract-review record on any head. Inputs:
- claim 6944041623, area hand-off 6948383268, takeover 6949036026;
- the card's Premise corrected 6943926042;
- the PR body;
- the net diff from merge-base `f6f5b50a` (38 files, +647 / -49);
- check-runs on this head.

The four markings read correct where they are made. The sentences name no field, id or API name. `record_not_found` reads the same for a missing row and a hidden one, which is what ruling 5985885287 requires. `code`, status and `message` do not move. One row is incomplete, and the surface needs paper.

### Must-fix

**M1. Seven paths fall outside the claimed surface, and the card has no amendment for them.** Claim 6944041623 names the catalog, the core helper, the listed `recordNotFoundError` call sites, the four query-field producers, the middleware, `lifecycle-hooks.ts`, tests beside each, and the changeset. The diff also moves:
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx` and `http-protocol.mdx` (the two `RECORD_NOT_FOUND` body examples);
- `packages/mcp/src/mcp-coded-refusal.test.ts` and `stdio-data-bridge.not-found.test.ts` (forced shape pins; `packages/mcp` is not in the claim at all);
- `packages/runtime/src/batch-row-http-status-real-driver.integration.test.ts` and `duplicate-record-user-message-doors-33790.test.ts` (forced; neither sits beside `action-execution.ts`);
- `packages/rest/src/record-field-access-route.test.ts` (forced; it tests `record-field-access-route.ts`, which is not a listed call site).

I read `protocol.batch-row-*.test.ts` and `record-lock-batch-row-status.integration.test.ts` as beside `protocol-batch-data.ts` and `lifecycle-hooks.ts`. Each of the seven is forced by the added field or documents it. Please post one amendment on #34699 that names them with their reasons, plus any path the S1 fix moves. The card thread is gone, so the area posts it.

### Should-fix

**S1. Row 3 is incomplete on the action and flow-start doors, and the body says the caller is out of reach there when it is not.** `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:4231`) still calls `recordNotFoundError(objectName, recordId ?? '')` with no caller. So a zh-CN user who runs an action on a record they cannot read, or on an id that names nothing, reads the English sentence. Three of its five callers hold the caller's context:
- `refuseDeniedSubjectBeforeHandOff` holds `wiring.ec` (`:3396`);
- `refuseUnreadableFlowStartRecords` holds `executionContext` (`:4525`);
- `executeDeclarativeUpdateAction` holds `wiring.ec` (`:4804`).

`refuseDeniedSubjectLoadBeforeDispatch` (`:4369`) takes none in its parameters, and `runtime/src/domains/mcp.ts:2311` is the MCP door the body already excludes. The body's "Not given a caller: … `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` … (no caller context in reach)" is wrong for the three callers above. The data door's own miss on the same object (`callData`, `:701`) now answers in zh-CN. Both answers are still the same for a missing row and a hidden one on each door, so this is not an existence oracle, only English where the card asks for the caller's language. Please do one of these:
- (a) give `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad` an optional caller and pass it from the three callers that hold one, with one zh-CN pin on the action door;
- (b) correct the body line and file the action and flow-start doors as a follow-up card under #34699.

(a) is a one-parameter change in a claimed file and closes the row the card names.

### Nits

- **N1 (for the contract review to rule; no change unless it asks).** `Clause-②: no` is declared. Yet `@objectstack/core` gains two public exports, `operationUserMessage` and the type `UserMessageCaller`, and `recordNotFoundError` gains an optional third parameter. The `/data` 404 body and the batch rows also gain a `userMessage` key. Precedent is split: #33524 (new catalog keys and a refusal's `userMessage`) declared `no`, while #33790 (a `userMessage` key on the 409 and on row errors) declared `yes (widening)`. The changeset level (`patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`) is right either way. The only thing that moves is the release-notes section (`docs/releases-maintenance.md`: 新增能力 against 其他修复).
- **N2.** `assertRecordExists` (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts:204`) passes no caller. Its two callers in `protocol-batch-data.ts` (`:468`, `:962`) hold `context`. The path only runs when the engine's update answered null without its own not-found throw, so it is rarely reached. This can be folded into S1 (a) if `protocol-record-reads.ts` joins the amendment; otherwise it becomes a card.

### Checklist (the rest holds)

- **Changeset:** it names all 11 published packages whose `src` moved (`spec`, `core`, `objectql`, `metadata-protocol`, `runtime`, `rest`, `plugin-security`, `plugin-approvals`, `plugin-audit`, `service-analytics`, `service-print`). `packages/mcp` moved only tests. `patch` with `Metadata-protocol: none` is the right level. The spec `api-surface` baseline does not move, which fits: the three keys are catalog strings, not exports.
- **Catalog:** the three keys are in `en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP` and `es-ES`, with no placeholders and no wire vocabulary. The test pins every locale, distinct texts, the fallback and a deployment override.
- **Producers:** the middleware marks the query-field refusal through its own `userFacingDenialMessage` (the deployment `errors.<key>` override applies) and marks only `PermissionDeniedError`. The delegated gate catch marks only a `DelegationScopeViolationError` answer, so the not-found that `readDoorAnswerForGateRefusal` can return keeps its own sentence. The three non-security producers leave the aggregate role unmarked, as the changeset says. The per-row record lock passes the localized sentence as `userMessage` without the `RECORD_LOCKED: ` prefix, and the bound refusals mark none.
- **Docs made false:** none. The two doc examples and the http-protocol ladder sentence match `operationUserMessage`.
- **Tests:** the new plugin-security file runs real `ObjectQL`, a real `SqlDriver` and the real `SecurityPlugin`, with zh-CN, workspace and `en` legs and a CONTROL. I read the six forced shape changes: each adds only the new key, except the #33790 CONTROL, which moves to a write that still marks nothing and keeps its assertion. The body's ablation table shows each leg red.
- **Gates at this head:** latest attempt per check, 70 runs: 58 `success`, 12 `skipped`, none failed.
- **Overlap:** the takeover's overlap check against main and #34817 / #34709 reads clean.

**Owed, for the seat:** a contract review at CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER. It is owed for the non-test `packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` path (three new catalog keys) and the core public export, and the claim and the body both say so. Please rule N1 there. On Tier H: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34811` reads NOT governed (0 of 38 paths, 696 lines). But the body's 维护者速读 tells the maintainer "Tier H 交 os-zhuang 批", and the claim's lane line says "seat Tier H". Please settle which applies and have the body say it. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.

This reviews the delta from L1 6949320766 (REWORK at `d50700b3`: M1, S1, N1, N2). Inputs:
- dev report 6953246841 and claim amendment 6952327352;
- the main merge `c7362a76`;
- the delta `c7362a76..1130a716` (8 files, +140 / -17), read line by line;

- **Merge:** the net diff over the PR's files from the merge-base to `d50700b3` is line-identical to main..`c7362a76`.

- **Body:** the false "no caller context in reach" line is gone. The maintainer summary now says NOT governed (0/43 paths, 849 lines), as the seat ruled, with no Tier H.

No new findings.

This ACCEPT does not stand in for those gates.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `1130a716e03ac4a5d701a143b5e821b892f9e104`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts + packages/core/src/utils/operation-user-message.ts, packages/core/src/utils/record-not-found.ts, packages/core/src/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/lifecycle-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/payload-predicate-guard.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts, packages/services/service-analytics/src/field-read-admission.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-dispatch.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-record-reads.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-batch-data.ts

First seat contract review of this PR: no earlier contract-review record exists on the PR or on card #34699 at any head, so this is a review of the whole net diff against `main` (43 files, +785 / -64), not a delta. Read 2026-11-17T16:20Z. Inputs: card #34699 with all 8 comments, the PR body, the net diff, the check-runs on this head. The remainder of the diff (tests, the one-argument call sites in objectql, rest, service-print, own-row-delete-routes, protocol-data-crud, protocol-data-writes, the two docs examples, the changeset) is the lane seat's ACCEPT (L1 delta 6953842787).

### ① Derived judgments

- Catalog accept-set: `BUILTIN_OPERATION_MESSAGES` gains `record_not_found`, `query_field_not_readable`, `delegation_scope_violation` in all four locales (`en`, `zh-CN`, `ja-JP`, `es-ES`). Additive; no existing key or text moves. Right.
- Public surface, `@objectstack/core`: new exports `operationUserMessage` and type `UserMessageCaller` (through `export *` in `index.ts`); `recordNotFoundError` gains an optional third parameter. Every two-argument caller still compiles and still gets a refusal. Right, a widening.
- Wire: `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` (every door built on `recordNotFoundError`, batch rows included), the `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` predicate refusal from its four producers, `403 DELEGATION_SCOPE_VIOLATION` and the per-row `409 RECORD_LOCKED` each gain one key, `userMessage`. `code`, status and `message` are byte-identical on every one: read at each throw site, none of the four `message` templates is edited. Right.
- Narrowing check, the question the order put: nothing a caller could see before is taken away or reworded. The only caller-visible change besides the added key is which text a client that prefers `userMessage` shows. On doors that pass no caller (the MCP data doors `mcp-http-tools.ts:3120`, `stdio-data-bridge.ts:1357/1391`, and `runtime/domains/mcp.ts`) the not-found now carries the English sentence where it carried none. That adds a key and removes nothing; the body discloses it. No narrowing.
- Existence hiding: `record_not_found` is one text for a missing row and a hidden one. On each door both answers are built from the same context (the middleware's hidden-row arms and the engine's missing-row arms both pass `opCtx.context`; the action and flow-start doors route both through `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad`), so the language cannot tell the two apart either. Right against ruling 5985885287.
- Language source, the other question: every marked refusal reads its locale off the operation's execution context and nothing else. `operationUserMessage` takes `caller.locale`, then `caller.workspaceLocale`, then `en`; the middleware's two markings take `denialLocalesOf(opCtx.context)`; the record lock takes `refusalLocalization(ctx, …)` as before. That context is filled by `assembleExecutionContext` (`locale: requestLocale ?? localization.locale`, `workspaceLocale: localization.locale`). No marking reads a process default, an env value or the row. An anonymous caller has neither rung and reads `en`, which is the existing ladder, not this PR's.
- Non-exported signatures widened by an optional parameter (`snapshotQueryRefusal`, `parentFieldQueryRefusal`, `fieldReadDeniedError`, `refuseDeniedSubjectLoad`, `refuseDeniedSubjectLoadBeforeDispatch`, `assertRecordExists`): none is named on its package index. Internal, right.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening). Declared on the PR body and in the changeset, identically, with `Metadata-protocol: none`.

- Correct: the diff adds exports and keys and removes or tightens nothing (① above), so `yes (widening)` is the true arm and `(narrowing)` is not owed.
- Complete as to what the order asked: the changeset names the three catalog keys, `operationUserMessage`, `UserMessageCaller` and the optional third argument of `recordNotFoundError`; its bullets name the four refusals that gain `userMessage`. I found no further export: the diff touches no `package.json`, no other package index, and no spec `api-surface` baseline (the keys are entries of an existing exported constant, so none moves).
- Level: `patch` on the 11 published packages whose `src` moved (`packages/mcp` moves tests only). An added optional parameter, two added exports and added catalog strings with `Metadata-protocol: none` fit `patch` under the repo's convention, as #33790 did. `Check Changeset`: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Dev flags and `open_questions`: report 6953246841 carries `open_questions: []`. Report 6946285187's one question (contract review owed, Tier H) is answered: this record is the contract review; `Governed Surface Queue Guard` is success and the takeover reads the PR NOT governed, so no Tier H approval is owed beyond it.
- Out-of-scope note 1 (the MCP `run_action` hand-off pre-check `subjectVerdictRefusal` rebuilds the refusal from `message`, status and code, so `userMessage` does not reach that MCP answer): read at `action-dispatch.ts:352`. It is the state before this PR, on a door outside the card's rows. Accepted as noted; a follow-up card if the MCP door is to answer the sentence.
- Out-of-scope note 2 (#34817 conflicts on `plugin-audit/src/parent-field-query-guard.ts`): a landing-order matter for the area, not a contract one.
- Deviation (the fourth call site, `action-dispatch.ts:701`): right. Without it the REST action door for script, body and flow actions would answer English, the row the card names.
- SQL push-down: the diff adds no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join. Each change is a parameter, a property on an error, or a string. Nothing to find.
- Gates, as concluded on this head at the read: success on `Lint & Repo Gates` and all its parts, `TypeScript Type Check` and all its parts, `Check Changeset`, `Spec property liveness`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core` 1 through 9 of 10, and 14 of 16 `Test UI` shards. NOT concluded green: `Test UI (3/16)` and `Test UI (11/16)` are `failure` (and so the `Test UI` roll-up), on tests under `ui/`, where this diff has no path; `Test Core (10/10)` was `in_progress`. This PASS is the design verdict and does not stand in for them: landing waits on the two UI shards re-run to green and on `Test Core (10/10)` concluding success. A second red on either UI shard is a real failure, not a flake.

### ④ Design judgment

No must-fix, no should-fix.

`packages/spec/src/system/operation-message.ts` (hits). Against the card as narrowed by Premise corrected 6943926042 (rows 1, 3, 4, 5 through the existing `userMessage` channel and this catalog, no second channel) and against its first consumers:
- The three keys are placeholder-free in every locale, and each producer renders them with no params, so no `{{…}}` can reach a user. The zh-CN texts read as natural end-user sentences and name no field, id, API name or wire code.
- `record_not_found` says both causes and decides neither, in all four locales. That is what the ruling requires of a text shown for both.
- `delegation_scope_violation` names no business unit or permission set; the gate's reason stays in `message`.
- Tried to break `query_field_not_readable` on the aggregate role, where "remove that condition" would be wrong advice. It holds: plugin-security refuses an aggregate over a hidden field earlier, at step 2.5b (`:1704`), unmarked; step 2.9, the marked one, is reached by a hidden field in `where`, `having`, `orderBy`, a find's `groupBy` or an aggregation's `filter`, which are conditions. The other three producers skip the marking on their aggregate arm, each pinned by a test.

Implementing files, sentence by sentence:
- `operation-user-message.ts`: the ladder is the one the docblock states and the one `denialLocaleOf` uses (first rung the built-in catalog carries, matched by `resolveBundleLocale`, else `en` through `renderOperationMessage`'s own fallback). A non-string or empty rung is skipped; `null` and no caller give `en`. Agrees.
- `record-not-found.ts`: `message`, `code`, `status`, `object` unchanged; `userMessage` always set. Agrees with the jsdoc and the docs examples.
